metadata.description: Verify radiational cooling signal is wired to daily HIGH temperature, not daily LOW

finding.detail: Radiational cooling signal is correctly wired to LOW markets (overnight minimum temperature), not HIGH markets (daily maximum). This is the correct physical behavior — radiational cooling on clear, calm nights depresses overnight minimums, not daytime maximums.
evidence: core/signals/radiational_cooling_signal.py line 18: '# LOW market only — radiational cooling depresses overnight minima.'
The signal's evaluate() method produces DOWN-direction predictions for LOW markets only
The signal is not registered in any HIGH-market pool
Radiational cooling affects overnight temperature minimum via longwave radiation loss under clear/calm/dry conditions — this is physically correct
For daily HIGH temperature trading, radiational_cooling_signal should NEVER fire. Pool routing in signal_fusion.py correctly excludes it from HIGH-market evaluation
finding.recommendation: No action needed. Signal is correctly scoped to LOW markets. If HIGH market relevance is desired, the signal would need to be re-engineered to detect post-radiational warming (inversion breakout).
